newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Economic Times
ESSAR, RELIANCE PETRO JOIN HANDS FOR PIPELINE PROJECT

Essar Oil and Reliance Petroleum finally agreed to jointly build a white oil pipeline between Vadinar and Kandla to evacuate petroleum products from their respective refineries at Jamnagar. Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) was expected to be the third partner with a majority stake in the pipeline joint venture. The two private companies have jointly sought the petroleum ministry's permission to include IOC in the venture. Essar and Reliance would have a 26 percent stake each in the project. IOC was expected to pick up the remaining 48 percent stake. The project was estimated to cost between three and four billion rupees, depending on the pipeline's route.
BUDGET TO SHORE UP INVESTOR SENTIMENTS

The Prime Minister indicated that the coming budget would have a package of measures to shore up investor sentiments. He was responding to a question on whether his interaction with world business leaders at the World Economic Forum in Davos had made him consider fresh measures in the budget.
SUMITOMO, MITSUBISHI WANT REVISED PROJECT CONTRACT

The engineering procurement construction (EPC) contractors of the 1040 mw Vizag power project, Sumitomo and Mitsubishi, have asked for a revision in the rupee content of the contract. The revision was asked taking into account inflation and the delay in executing the project. The project, one of the fast-track power projects being developed by the Hinduja National Power Company has been unable to finalise its fuel supply agreement despite protracted negotiations. Sources said the contractors, who had committed themselves to a contract price, felt if the project was delayed for long, the price quoted by them would not give them adequate returns.
Financial Express
REGULATOR SETS UNIFORM DAILY PRICE BANDS

The bourse regulator (SEBI) has imposed a uniform daily price band of a maximum of 10 percent on stock prices across all bourses. However, the overall weekly limit of 25 percent would remain. Except for scrips of value up to 20 rupees, price bands were at the discretion of the bourses. The SEBI chief said the daily price band was decided thus because different bourses were not following a system of daily price bands, resulting in volatility in the market.
Business Standard
BOMBAY BOURSE SURGES ON SPECULATIVE PURCHASES

The Bombay bourse sensitive index (sensex) rose by 53.41 points on speculative buying. It closed the day at 3,377.63 points, a gain of 1.58 percent from the previous day's close. The sensex opened at 3,322.04 and touched a high of 3,379.33. Market sources, though optimistic, were uncertain about the reason for the sudden spurt.
GOVERNMENT TO PUSH COAL, OIL SECTOR REFORMS

The government was planning a new set of proposals to restructure the coal sector, draft an oil exploration policy and recast the Sick Industrial Companies Act. The government would also decide on the dereservation of the small-scale sector, and the hike in levy price of sugar. Sources in the Prime Minister's Office said a compromise was also being worked out on the issue of foreign investment in the civil aviation sector. These would be taken up by the cabinet and the government would draft the necessary legislations for parliament's approval.
BROADCAST BILL TO BAR FOREIGNERS

The government proposed to repeal the law governing the cable television, in view of a comprehensive legislation on broadcasting slated to be introduced soon. It was also suggested that foreigners, advertising agencies, political parties, firms not incorporated in India, and religious organisations should not be allowed to get into the business of radio or television broadcast. In case of direct-to-home television services, all channels receivable from the satellite system used by the licensee should either be licensed or permitted by the proposed independent regulatory authority.
The Observer
NO ACCORD ON UNIFORM SETTLEMENT

Major bourses failed to adopt an uniform settlement cycle at the meeting of the executive committee of the inter exchange co-ordination group. The meeting was convened by the bourse regulator (SEBI). The matter would now be referred to a special committee, which would examine the feasibility of having a uniform settlement cycle across all the bourses.
Business Line
SUZUKI LOSING GROUND IN TAKEOVER BID

Suzuki Motor Corporation of Japan, the 50 percent equity partner in Maruti Udyog (MUL), getting desperate to wrest control of the company, was fighting a losing battle. The government was the other partner in the joint venture. The present Managing Director and Suzuki nominee would have to hand over charge to the government's nominee on August 28, 1997. This was in accordance to an agreement between the two partners to manage the affairs of the joint venture by rotation. With MUL on the verge of embarking on a massive expansion and modernisation plan, this was a situation the Japanese partner desperately wanted to avoid, sources said.
9.76 PCT RISE IN GENERAL INDEX

The latest index of industrial production (IIP) data released by the Central Statistical Organisation indicated a robust 9.76 percent increase in the general index. This increase was for the first seven months of the current fiscal over April-October 1995 and a 9.88 percent point-to-point growth rate for October 1996. Moreover, the growth performance was consistently good throughout the year so far, with the general IIP going up by 8.07 percent in April, 10.55 percent in May, 9.57 percent in June, 8.29 percent in July, 12.50 percent in August and 9.45 percent in September.
